description: Tier 2 diagnostic. Is the PAN and MnT control plane healthy? Node state, certificates, backup and patching first, then node resources, then the MnT collection that feeds every other dashboard.

panels.description: Deployment nodes in any state other than Connected. A PAN out of sync stops configuration reaching the deployment; an MnT out of sync stops every reporting panel in this dashboard set from advancing.

targets.expr: count(((ise3_deployment_node_state{state!="Connected"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="deployment"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="deployment"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="deployment"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="deployment"} == 1))) == 1))) == 1)

panels.title: Nodes not connected

panels.description: Whether automatic PAN failover is enabled. Without it, losing the primary admin node is a manual promotion under pressure rather than an automatic one.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: (ise3_deployment_pan_ha_enabled) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="deployment"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="deployment"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="deployment"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="deployment"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: PAN high availability

panels.description: Hours since the last successful configuration backup, and whether a backup schedule is configured at all. A daily backup that has not run is the earliest visible sign of a stalled PAN, so age goes amber at 26 hours rather than waiting for a failure — and 'not configured' is a different problem from 'stale', which is why both are here.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: (ise3_backup_age_hours) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="backup"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="backup"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="backup"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="backup"} == 1))) == 1))

(ise3_backup_configured) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="backup"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="backup"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="backup"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="backup"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Backup state

panels.description: Certificates in the deployment's trust and system stores that are already past their expiry date. Any number above zero is red: an expired EAP or admin certificate breaks authentication outright.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: (ise3_certificates_expired) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="certificates"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="certificates"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="certificates"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="certificates"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Certificates expired

panels.description: Share of this dashboard's own datasets that both collected successfully and are inside their freshness window (backup, certificates, deployment). Below 100% means some panel here is blank or stale, and the pipeline dashboard says which.

targets.expr: avg(((max by (dataset) (ise3_dataset_up{dataset=~"deployment|certificates|backup"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset=~"deployment|certificates|backup"} == 1))) == bool 1) * ((max by (dataset) (ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset=~"deployment|certificates|backup"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset=~"deployment|certificates|backup"} == 1))) == bool 1))

panels.title: Data trustworthy

panels.description: Time since the least recently collected of this dashboard's datasets last succeeded. Every number on this page is at least this old; a value climbing past its collection interval means ISE is answering slowly or not at all.

targets.expr: max(time() - (max by (dataset) (ise3_dataset_last_success_timestamp{dataset=~"deployment|certificates|backup"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset=~"deployment|certificates|backup"} == 1))))

panels.title: Collection age

panels.description: One lane per deployment node, green while ISE reported it Connected. The single most useful panel during a control plane incident: it shows exactly when a node left and whether it came back.

targets.expr: sum by (node) ((ise3_deployment_node_state{state="Connected"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="deployment"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="deployment"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="deployment"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="deployment"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Node connection state

panels.description: Certificates inside the exporter's warning horizon but not yet expired. This is the number that should be worked down to zero through change control; the expired count on the strip above is what happens when it is not.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: (ise3_certificates_expiring_soon) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="certificates"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="certificates"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="certificates"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="certificates"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Certificates expiring soon

panels.description: Nodes the certificate scan read, and nodes it could not reach. Certificates on an unreachable node are counted nowhere on this page, so a non-zero second value means the expiry numbers here are incomplete rather than clean.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: (ise3_certificate_nodes_scanned) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="certificates"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="certificates"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="certificates"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="certificates"} == 1))) == 1))

(ise3_certificate_nodes_unreachable) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="certificates"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="certificates"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="certificates"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="certificates"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Certificate scan coverage

panels.description: The deployment's patch level, and whether the running release is one this exporter and Cisco still support. Unsupported means schema drift is expected and some panels may quietly stop being populated.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: (ise3_patch_level) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="patches"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="patches"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="patches"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="patches"} == 1))) == 1))

(ise3_version_supported) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="patches"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="patches"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="patches"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="patches"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Patch level and release support

panels.description: Every node with the personas and services ISE has assigned to it. Read it when the deployment is not behaving as designed — a service running where it should not be, or missing where it should, explains a surprising amount.

targets.expr: (ise3_deployment_node_service_enabled) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="deployment"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="deployment"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="deployment"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="deployment"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Node roles and services

panels.description: Every certificate the scan could read, with days remaining. Red inside 30 days, amber inside 90 — enough notice to renew through change control rather than at 3am. Sorted ascending so the next thing to expire is always the first row.

targets.expr: (ise3_certificate_expiry_days) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="certificates"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="certificates"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="certificates"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="certificates"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Certificate expiry, soonest first

panels.description: Per-node CPU across the whole deployment, PAN and MnT included. An MnT pinned at high CPU is the usual reason reporting data goes stale while ISE itself keeps authenticating normally.

targets.expr: (ise3_node_cpu_utilization_percent) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="psn_performance"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="psn_performance"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="psn_performance"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="psn_performance"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: CPU utilisation

panels.description: Per-node memory across the deployment. Sustained pressure on an admin node shows up as slow configuration changes long before it shows up as an outage.

targets.expr: (ise3_node_memory_utilization_percent) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="psn_performance"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="psn_performance"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="psn_performance"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="psn_performance"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Memory utilisation

panels.description: The fullest filesystem on each node. On an MnT this is the one to watch: when its log partition fills, ISE purges aggressively and the reporting views lose history without any error being raised.

targets.expr: max by (node) ((ise3_node_disk_utilization_percent) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="psn_performance"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="psn_performance"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="psn_performance"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="psn_performance"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Disk utilisation, worst filesystem per node

panels.description: Mean and worst-case authentication time reconstructed from MnT session detail. This is the number to quote when someone says logging in is slow, and the step breakdown below says which phase is responsible.

targets.expr: (ise3_session_authentication_latency_seconds{statistic="mean"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1))

(ise3_session_authentication_latency_seconds{statistic="max"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: End-to-end authentication latency

panels.description: Mean time in each phase of the authentication exchange, with how many sessions contributed. A step whose sample count is small is not evidence — read the two columns together before concluding anything from a slow phase.

targets.expr: (ise3_session_authentication_step_latency_seconds{statistic="mean"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1))

(ise3_session_authentication_step_latency_samples) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Authentication step latency

panels.description: How much of the live session list the exporter has fetched per-session detail for. Panels fed from that detail are suppressed below 99% so they cannot under-report beside a complete neighbour — this panel is where the gap is visible.

targets.expr: ise3_detail_cache_coverage{cache="mnt_session_detail"}

panels.title: MnT detail-cache coverage

panels.description: The status ISE recorded for the last backup attempt, and how long ago it succeeded. Read it when the age stat is amber: a failed status is a backup target problem, no status at all is a scheduler problem on the PAN.

targets.expr: (ise3_backup_last_status) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="backup"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="backup"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="backup"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="backup"} == 1))) == 1)) == 1

time() - ((ise3_backup_last_success_timestamp) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="backup"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="backup"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="backup"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="backup"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Backup history

panels.description: The most recent failure recorded for each of the control plane datasets, with the reason and the detail the exporter captured. Empty is the healthy state; a populated row is the actual error text rather than a generic failure count.

targets.expr: ise3_dataset_last_failure_detail_info{dataset=~"deployment|backup|certificates|patches|licensing"}

panels.title: Control plane collection failures

panels.description: Purpose, reading order, and where to go next. Kept with the dashboard so the meaning cannot drift away from the panels.

options.content:
**Purpose** — answer whether the administration and monitoring plane is healthy — the nodes, their certificates, their backups, and the MnT pipeline the rest of the set depends on.

**Read it in this order**

1. Read the status strip. Anything red here undermines dashboards elsewhere.
2. Check the node connection timeline for when a node left.
3. Read certificate expiry ascending — the first row is the next thing that will break.

**When something is red**

- MnT disk or CPU high: reporting data across every dashboard is about to go stale.
- Backup stale: check the PAN before assuming it is a backup target problem.
- Certificates expired: RADIUS access will already be showing certificate failure classes.

**Related dashboards** — Triage, RADIUS access, PSN service, Capacity

*Owner: set this to the team that answers the page. Runbook: link it here — a red panel with no runbook is a puzzle, not an alert.*
